title: How did potato blight first reach Europe in the 1840s?
short: Potato blight helped set off the Irish famine. A shipping record and a farmer’s letter could show how the disease first reached a European field.
matters: Preserved leaves have allowed researchers to identify a lineage of the organism that caused late blight during the Irish famine. Historians have also traced efforts in West Flanders to obtain potatoes from the Americas. What is missing is a documented connection between a particular arrival and an early report from a field.
stuck: A ship could call at several ports, and a potato bought in one country could have been grown in another. A cargo list records what a merchant declared. A later account of the first damage may give the date when the news reached a city.
solved: A named vessel, dated cargo record and independent record of delivery to a grower with early blight would make a strong historical case. Compare North American and Andean candidates and show where each paper trail ends.
approach: Begin with the documented West Flanders imports and trace consignments through port notices, customs books and agricultural correspondence for 1843–45.
Check reports of seed potatoes and of potatoes travelling alongside other cargo, including Peruvian guano. Record what the source actually lists.
Date the earliest field reports in Belgium, Britain and Ireland from their original publications. Compare shipment dates, local destinations and gaps in the records.

needs.ask: Link customs and newspaper notices to estate or agricultural society records of receipt.
Locate the farms and ports in the earliest dated reports, including uncertain place identifications.
